NEW DELHI: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee on Tuesday shared a picture with AISA leader Neha Bora amid protests taking place against Election Commission chief Gyanesh Kumar.Rathee and Bora shared the picture on X, showing them seated on a sofa under the portraits of of BR Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi. On Instagram, Rathee posted the picture with the caption, “with our tigress”, referring to Bora.The YouTuber-activist and the student leader were detained on October 10, when the Abhijeet Dipke-led CJP planned a major demonstration demanding Gyanesh's resignation over the Election Commission’s conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.However, a large-scale security deployment and a crackdown on protesters curtailed the demonstration in the national capital.More than 30,000 personnel were deployed, while over 7,000 people were detained across the city, according to the figures cited.Calls for CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation extend beyond the youth-led CJP, with the opposition, led by Rahul Gandhi , also stepping up its campaign against the poll body chief.The INDIA bloc has raised concerns over the Election Commission’s conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The opposition bloc also moved the Supreme Court, flagging its concerns over Gyanesh and the poll body’s functioning.Neha Bora was also at the forefront of opposition's protest against poll body chief.

A large-scale security deployment and a crackdown on protesters curtailed the demonstration in the national capital. Rathee posted the picture with the caption, “with our tigress”, referring to Bora.

Article Title: 'Don’t want to spoil the surprise': Rahul Gandhi on INDIA bloc's next step in CEC-SIR row
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday said he does not want to reveal the opposition's next step amid the CEC-SIR row, saying that revealing the strategy would spoil excitement and sense of surprise for the citizens of the country."Sooner or later, whether tomorrow, the day after, in three months, six months, a year, or two years, it (protests) will not stop. It will reach the end goal. I cannot tell you exactly how we will get there, because that would spoil the surprise, and we want to maintain the excitement and sense of surprise for you and the country," Rahul Gandhi told reporters at a joint briefing of opposition parties at his residence, where he hosted them for evening tea.The Lok Sabha leader of opposition asserted that the Congress-led INDIA bloc would continue its fight against the government with the same energy, strength and unity with which it mobilised for the protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls exercise.Rahul Gandhi also thanked the Supreme Court and Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, while asserting that the political resistance would continue.ALSO READ: High tea after street heat: What happened at INDIA bloc meet at Rahul Gandhi's residence "Thank you to the Supreme Court—we have immense respect for the Supreme Court, the Chief Justice of India, and the Indian judicial system. They have a role to play, and we hope they will play it. However, we are political people; no matter what happens, or which institution plays a role or doesn't, political resistance will continue, people's resistance will continue, and it will triumph," the Congress MP added.Rahul Gandhi's remarks came a day after he, along with 10 other opposition leaders, filed a plea in the Supreme Court in the matter, naming the Election Commission (EC), CEC Kumar, and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, as respondents.Kumar has come under scrutiny since The Indian Express reported last month that Sandhu and Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those related to the SIR.ALSO READ: 'Absence from draft SIR doesn't mean deletion': EC to Bombay HC In response, the EC said differences were "common" in multi-member institutions and maintained that all decisions were ultimately taken unanimously by the three commissioners.The poll body is required to take decisions either unanimously or by a 2-1 majority.Since becoming CEC in 2025, a year after his appointment to the commission, Kumar has repeatedly faced allegations of favouring the ruling BJP.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi does not want to reveal the opposition's next step amid the CEC-SIR row. He says revealing the strategy would spoil excitement and sense of surprise for the citizens of the country. Gandhi also thanked the Supreme Court and Chief Justice of India Surya Kant.

NEW DELHI: INDIA bloc leaders gathered at Rahul Gandhi 's residence on Tuesday for high tea amid their ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote theft. They met for a high tea after four days of protest and filing a petition in SC against the CEC.From directly slamming the CEC to criticising the SIR process and criticising PM Modi and Amit Shah, several leaders including Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Supriya Sule, Tejashwi Yadav, Sanjay Raut addressed a press conference after the meet vowing to continue their protests while giving insights into what they decided at the meeting.Here's what some of the key leaders saidLeader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi anonunced that the INDIA bloc would continue its fight to restore the democratic process and ensure accountability for those he accused of undermining it. "We are all standing here together as one. As I said yesterday, there are no parallel protests. There is one singular protest, and the protest has one mission: restoration of democracy in India.Democracy has been destroyed in this country. The election system has been destroyed. The Constitution has been torn up and thrown away. We are fighting together to restore democratic rule, genuine democratic rule in this country."He thanked people who supported the protest and vowed to bring those responsible to justice. "It is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice.""Yesterday, you saw an expression not of the political party standing here, but an expression of the people of India...We would like to thank the people of Delhi, the people of India, who stood with us against what is being done. This is not about us. This is about the people of India. This is about the future of the people of India, and we, all of us together, because we love you and we respect you, are going to fight to the end to restore the democratic process in this country. It is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice," he added.Further assuring the work of the team, the Congress leader said, "I used the word 'perseverance' at the press conference yesterday—that this team of ours is not going to stop. Sooner or later—whether tomorrow, the day after, in three months, six months, a year, or two years—it will not stop. It will reach the end goal. I cannot tell you exactly how we will get there, because that would spoil the surprise, and we want to maintain the excitement and sense of surprise for you and the country. But I guarantee you that just as we mobilized—with such energy, strength, and unity—we will continue to fight together in the same spirit. Thank you to the Supreme Court—we have immense respect for the Supreme Court, the Chief Justice of India, and the Indian judicial system; they have a role to play, and we hope they will play it. However, we are political people; no matter what happens, or which institution plays a role or doesn't, political resistance will continue, people's resistance will continue, and it will triumph."The Congress president hailed INDIA bloc protests against "vote chori", CEC as "massive success". "We will carry forward this united fight (protests) against Modi govt, "vote chori", he said.Giving highlights of what they decided in the meeting, he said, "We held a meeting with senior leaders of the INDIA bloc, where we discussed the current situation in the country and how to take forward the campaign demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."Further slamming the decision to de ntoify Jantar Mantar as a protest site, he added, "The government has now denotified Jantar Mantar. We strongly condemn this decision. Jantar Mantar must remain a place where people can protest.""Gyanesh Kumar has joined the ruling party's team... He steals votes, protest site and democracy," said CPI(M) leader M A Baby after the INDIA bloc meeting ."(CEC) Gyanesh Kumar is a "mafia" who has criminalised entire system; we know how to fight such mafia," he said. Further talking about the meeting, he added, "Rahul ji had convened it and invited everyone—leaders and MPs were present for the high tea—and it was a very good meeting. Discussions were held, and everyone's suggestions regarding the way forward and their respective views were taken into account; however, the ongoing struggle against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Modi ji, and Shah ji will continue—both in the national capital and elsewhere. "She accused the Election Commission of undermining free and fair elections. She demanded a halt to the SIR process, restoration of previous electoral rolls, Kumar’s removal and criminal proceedings against officials allegedly involved in electoral irregularities."Every day, it is becoming increasingly clear that the Gyanesh Kumar-led Election Commission is undermining free and fair elections in India. As long as the Gyanesh Kumar-led Election Commission continues to function, there will be no free and fair elections in India. We stand completely united with all the leaders and parties of the INDIA alliance. We will not stop until Mr Gyanesh Kumar is removed and criminal proceedings are initiated not only against him but also against all Election Commission officials who supervised elections in Haryana, Maharashtra, Bengal and Bihar, because these have been elections marked by vote chori," she said."The government currently in power in Bengal is illegitimate. It came to power through vote chori...We have a set of demands: halt the SIR process, stop it and revert to the old electoral rolls. Gyanesh Kumar must be dismissed, and criminal proceedings must be initiated against him. All officials, who have been involved in vote chori, must be investigated, and criminal proceedings must be initiated against them. We will not rest until this Election Commission is held accountable," she added.Sule expressed solidarity against the CEC and stated that their agitation will continue. "We stand united with full strength as part of the INDIA alliance; our struggle will continue because the Constitution has been undermined and is currently in danger in this country. We will persist with our agitation to uphold the rights granted to all Indians in the Constitution by Bharat Ratna Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar. A single individual—representing a single government—is making a grave mistake by attempting to trample upon these rights. We stand united with full strength to fight against this injustice and oppression; our movement will continue, from Delhi down to the grassroots level," she said.Taking aim at the govt said, "Govt's vote chori exposed before people. We are all together and will win." Criticising the move to remove Jantar Mantar as a protest site, he added, "Govt's fear is evident in denotification of Jantar Mantar as protest site."She directly took at aim at the BJP and said, "The one enemy of the people of this country, of Indian democracy, and of the Constitution is the BJP.An attack on voter rights is an attack on India and an attack on democracy.CEC Gyanesh Kumar must go.The SIR process is compromised."
Article Summary: India bloc leaders gathered at Rahul Gandhi's residence on Tuesday for high tea amid their ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote theft. Leaders including Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Supriya Sule, Tejashwi Yadav, Sanjay Raut addressed a press conference after the meet vowing to continue their protests while giving insights into what they decided at the meeting.

Article Title: 'It's a no-brainer': EAM Jaishankar underlines need for stable border for normal ties with China
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Tuesday said that if China wants a normal relationship with New Delhi, the border between the two countries has to be stable.During a conversation at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, Jaishankar said that India and China do not have an agreed border and that the issue has persisted for decades."We don't have an agreed border between India and China. This is not a new issue; it's been going on for multiple decades... From 1975 till 2020, a good 45 years, no blood was shed on that border. The last time there were fatalities was in 1975. In this period, India-China relations did grow," he said."Then in 2020, when we were in the midst of the Covid lockdown, we had a series of border issues, and it culminated in a clash in which a number of soldiers were killed on either side," Jaishankar added.Jaishankar said that if peace and tranquillity in the border areas are disturbed, then the relationship will have consequences."For us, what it represented was a very profound departure from the situation that was prevailing since 1975. If the peace and tranquillity in the border areas are disturbed, then the relationship will have consequences. Those consequences were very visible for the next five years until we were able to restore the peace and tranquillity.It took four years of negotiations," he added."The point we make to the Chinese is: 'If you want a normal relationship, if the rest of the relationship is to move, it's common sense. It's a no-brainer that the boundary has to be stable, that we need peace and tranquillity in the border areas.' As the border areas are settling down, they have settled down to a great extent since 2024; the relationship is commensurately moving towards normalcy," he further said.This comes after the ministry of external affairs reiterated that the Union territory of Ladakh is an integral and inalienable part of India after the Chinese foreign ministry opposed the naming of certain strategic locations in Ladakh."The announcement mentions that the twenty-eight (28) places/features located in the UT of Ladakh have been identified with standard place and feature names on the official map of Survey of India, and it has been done in consultation with the Union Territory of Ladakh and local stakeholders," MEA said."Identifying these places formally on the Survey of India map of UT of Ladakh is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large," the ministry said.On October 2, India formally identified 28 strategic locations and geographical features in Ladakh on its official map, including key border friction points along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), such as Gogra and Hot Spring.The move, undertaken in consultation with the Ladakh administration, aimed to improve official mapping, ensure precise identification and raise public awareness of the sensitive border region.
Article Summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar said that if China wants a normal relationship with New Delhi, the border between the two countries has to be stable. The last time there were fatalities was in 1975, he said. India formally identified 28 strategic locations and geographical features in Ladakh on its official map, including key border friction points.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi peddling lies on SIR to cover Congress poll defeats: Amit Shah
Article Text:
Shah: BJP victories in ballot paper civic polls lesson for Rahul

NEW DELHI: Going on the offensive amid opposition's stir against special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Union home minister Amit Shah Tuesday accused Rahul Gandhi of fabricating lies about the exercise to hide his failure resulting in a string of Congress defeats, and to protect "infiltrators" who have been registered as voters."You and not SIR is responsible for Congress's defeats. Since you emerged as the main leader of Congress and then became its president and the leader of opposition, Congress has continuously lost elections. You should introspect," he said, asking the main opposition party and its allies to prepare themselves for a fourth consecutive defeat in the 2029 Lok Sabha polls."In many states you have not been able to win election for decades," Shah said, citing Congress's barren electoral performance in a number of states, including in Gujarat, Tripura, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, while SIR had started only after 2024.This is the first time Shah has taken on the opposition, which has been trying to ratchet up pressure for CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation through its street campaigns in the national capital, and signalled a determined intent of the BJP brass to challenge its opponents' allegation that Election Commission (EC) is working to benefit the party in polls.The framing of opposition's protests as an attempt to cover "infiltrators" is significant, as BJP has for long accused its opponents of helping illegal immigrants from Bangladesh as well as Rohingya from Myanmar getting registered as voters as part of their "votebank" politics.With opposition parties coming together, BJP and JD(U) held a joint press conference where Union minister Piyush Goyal dared opposition-run govts in different states to quit if it considered polls following SIR rigged.Union minister and JD(U) functionary Lalan Singh said the entire campaign is not for saving democracy but weakening it by targeting constitutional institutions and trying to stoke anarchy through street protests. The two ministers echoed Shah on Congress's poor show in UP, Bihar and Tamil Nadu for decades, and said it is not even a key party in vast swathes of the country.Union home minister Amit Shah's sharp comments came after BJP notched up another facile win in three local body polls in Gujarat, leaving Congress far behind. Aam Aadmi Party lost deposits in all 32 seats it contested in Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation, he noted.This win coupled with BJP and its allies' similar impressive show in local body polls in Tripura and Rajasthan, besides in the recent assembly and LS bypolls, demonstrated that people of the country are standing with PM Modi, BJP, and NDA like a rock, Shah said.Many of these polls were held through ballot papers, he said, as the opposition has often blamed EVMs for its losses. "These elections are a lesson for Rahul Gandhi... You (Rahul) cannot win the confidence of people by fabricated media events, 'jhooth ki goonj'," Shah said, riffing on Rahul's "Chhatron ki Goonj" outreach to students in different cities.Mocking the opposition's march in New Delhi on Monday, he said Rahul Gandhi cannot become the voice of the people by mobilising cadres of 14 parties to collect a crowd of 8,000 through a distance of 1.5km. They have no reach in the vast hinterland, he added. "Your negative politics will not benefit you. You should connect with people," he added.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah accused Rahul Gandhi of fabricating lies about the exercise to hide his failure resulting in a string of Congress defeats. This is the first time Shah has taken on the opposition, which has been trying to ratchet up pressure for CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.

Omair Ahmad is the author of ‘Encounters’, ‘The Storyteller's Tale’, ‘Tall Tales by a Small Dog’, ‘The Kingdom at the Centre of the World: Journeys Into Bhutan’ and ‘Jimmy, The Terrorist’, which won the Crossword Award for Fiction and was shortlisted for the Man Asian Literary Prize. He is also a prominent columnist and a political and social commentator. In this conversation, he discusses his latest novel, ‘Homecoming’. Excerpts:The genesis of this was when I was in DC. I just finished my second master's and I was missing home. Being a brown guy with a Muslim name in America, just when the war on terror was at its apogee leaves you a little off the place. And I hadn't been able to travel home since I’d gone, which was in 2001. So I met this person, a friend, and she invited me to a book club and everyone was writing little bits and they asked me to write something. And so I wrote the beginning of this novella, which is no longer the beginning. Much has changed, everything has changed. But there is a strong emotion behind it and I think that has carried through even now... My wife says it's about love, loss and Lucknow. I've gone very much for mood and the feel of a place.So there's a bit of history, there's. But it's largely about people. So there's characters I've known, characters I've imagined, bits of stories that I've heard about Lucknow.This was one of those things that I really struggled with. The novel as a form is very much a product of the European enlightenment pathway. It has the individual at the centre... If you pick up most novels, it's a very narrow thing of who they are. But for me, as a product of this country, of this culture, I always wanted to know what's behind them. Because we always understand people as being part of this family, this mahalla, this web of relationships. No person just is a person standing on their own... They are so much more than a person. They're also part of the past. They're also part of the relationship in their environments... The idea of the novel as a European construct and the way that we communicate is sometimes different, and we think that that's wrong. But I think one of the things which I have improved on is I'm no longer very apologetic about that. This is who I am. This is who we are. This is how we tell our stories...We are multilingual people. We talk in lots of languages. Even like, say, the Urdu or Hindi that I use at home and on the street and with elders versus young. These are all almost different languages. The way we use them, trying to transpose that into any language.. you're really struggling, because the forms aren't there. There's no correct way to go about it... I know that while I'm writing in English, I'm not necessarily thinking in English when I'm writing. And I'm writing about people who will be only partially thinking in English, if at all, or speaking in it. And so it's guesswork. It's just trying to bully my way through somehow to make this language work like that.Things are clearer in our memories than they were in real life. And if you ever had an argument with anybody, you know this true. Because in your memory, your argument is very clear. And in their memory, the argument is very clear. The reality is it was never clear. It was always messy.But there is truth there. And memory is important for us, especially as a country where so much of our history is actually oral history. And so much of our history has been badly reinterpreted by colonial administrators for their own design, and that we have swallowed wholesale. And then we spend our whole time... like how you take fish bones out once you've taken a bite... But I struggle with this because I don't know what is true in all of this. And I wanted to register that little thing that, yes, we think our memories are clearer than what is recorded, but should we be that trusting of our own memories or other people's memories as well?
Article Summary: Omair Ahmad is the author of ‘Encounters’, ‘The Storyteller's Tale’ and ‘Tall Tales by a Small Dog’ ‘Jimmy, The Terrorist’ won the Crossword Award for Fiction and was shortlisted for the Man Asian Literary Prize. He is also a prominent columnist and a political and social commentator. In this conversation he discusses his latest novel, 'Homecoming'

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

-

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: “I would never say never”: Tom Brady opens up about a new career possibility as his business empire continues to grow

Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, had been a force to be reckoned with on the field when he was playing. Ever since he retired from the league, the NFL legend Tom Brady has turned into a sports analyst for ESPN and has also become a popular entrepreneur. Amid this, it seems the NFL icon could also be interested in another career.A few weeks ago, the seven time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady walked the ramp for luxury brand, Gucci, in New York City’s Times Square as he turned heads.In an interview with GQ, the NFL icon reflected on if he is open to a career in fashion as he said, “I would never say never to doing anything, so if there was an opportunity that presented itself that I thought was really fun and new, I would definitely be open to it. I always say the only place for growth is outside your comfort zone, and I think this was one of those things: doing something that I had never really done on a big stage with some really great people. ”The New England Patriot’ legend also opened op about his fashion choices as he added, “I’ve always paid attention to a degree—I’ve been to plenty of Met Galas in my life, and I’ve always enjoyed stylish men’s clothing and suits—but I played it by ear on this particular occasion.”The 48 year old NFL icon added, “I don’t come in with any preconceived notions. Article Title: Asian Para Games: Defending champion Shailesh Kumar ready for another big jump
Article Text:
Shailesh Kumar

KOLKATA: There was a time when people in his village wondered what future awaited him.Unable to walk properly since childhood after being diagnosed with polio in his right leg, Shailesh Kumar, a resident of Islamnagar village in Bihar’s Jamui district, often faced doubts about what he could achieve.Today, the same people urge him to bring glory to the country, thanks to the success he has achieved in para-athletics. The T63 high jumper heads to the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as the defending champion, carrying not just expectations but also the confidence that comes from changing lives, including his own.“Life has changed significantly, both financially and socially. Earlier, people would wonder what I could achieve because I couldn’t walk properly. Today, their mindset has changed. They see that a para athlete can represent the country and achieve success,” Shailesh told TOI ahead of the Games.Since winning gold with a Games record at the 2023 Asian Para Games in China, the 26-year-old has added several major titles to his résumé, including gold medals at 2025 World Para Athletics Championships and 2026 World Para Athletics Grand Prix.Training under close friend and coach Ronak Malik in Bengaluru since Jan 2025, the 26-year-old is now focused on defending his high jump title.He enters the competition after overcoming knee issues that troubled him earlier in the season, but Malik is confident his ward can retain the gold medal in high jump and also contend for a podium finish in long jump.“If everything goes according to plan, he has the potential to win medals in both events. Gold is definitely a possibility. He has already set records at the World Championships and Asian Championships and has achieved personal best performances,” said Malik, a former national-level high jumper.Training a para athlete requires a different approach from coaching able-bodied athletes, and Malik regularly consults experienced jump coach GV Gaonkar to fine-tune Shailesh’s programme.While Malik’s guidance has proved hugely beneficial on the field, their friendship has also played a key role in Shailesh’s resurgence, particularly after Paris Paralympics, where he narrowly missed a medal and finished fourth.“After beginning his training in Sonipat in 2019, Shailesh moved to SAI Gandhinagar under coach Vinod Chauhan. Unfortunately, Vinod sir passed away in a road accident in April 2023. It was a difficult phase for Shailesh and he wasn’t in the best frame of mind going into the Paris Paralympics,” Malik said.It was after Chauhan’s death that Shailesh reconnected with Malik. Together, they are now targeting success not only at the Asian Para Games but also at next year’s World Championships and, ultimately, the Paralympics in LA.But as Malik says, none of it would have been possible without the discipline and dedication of Shailesh, who chose sport even as his family hoped he would focus on studies and secure a stable job.“People had different opinions about me, so I wanted to do something different. My family stood by me throughout and today they are very proud,” said Shailesh.But as he prepares for another Asian Para Games campaign, he remains determined not to be weighed down by expectations. “I am the defending champion, but I am an athlete first. When you represent the country there is pressure, but I try to keep it to a minimum and perform freely,” he said.For Shailesh, though, the biggest motivation remains the journey itself. From being doubted because of his disability to becoming a champion who inspires others, he believes para-sports have given him a life he never imagined, and he intends to make the most of it.
Article Summary: Shailesh Kumar is the defending champion of the T63 high jump at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The 26-year-old was diagnosed with polio in his right leg as a child. He has won several major titles, including gold medals at 2025 World Para Athletics Championships and 2026 World ParA Athletics Grand Prix.

Article Title: “I’ve often felt that people have no regard for..”: How Naomi Osaka turned her $15,000 French Open fine into a powerful push for mental health support
Article Text:
Naomi Osaka turned her $15,000 French Open fine into a powerful push for mental health support(Getty Images)

Naomi Osaka wanted her $15,000 French Open fine to support mental health

Naomi Osaka’s French Open withdrawal put athlete mental health in the spotlight

Naomi Osaka wanted the French Open to take athletes’ mental health more seriously. In May 2021, the tennis star announced that she would skip mandatory news conferences because of the pressure they placed on players. She also hoped the fines for missing those appearances would support mental health charities. What began as a protest over media duties soon became a much bigger conversation about the cost of competing at the highest level.The French Open fined Osaka $15,000 on May 30, 2021, after she skipped a news conference following her first-round win. A day later, she withdrew from the tournament after officials warned of harsher penalties. Osaka’s decision brought fresh attention to the pressure athletes face away from competition and her request to turn the fine into support for mental health.Before the tournament, Osaka explained her decision in a social media statement. She wrote, “I’ve often felt that people have no regard for athletes’ mental health and this rings very true whenever I see a press conference or partake in one.”The statement, shared ahead of the 2021 French Open, explained why she wanted to step away from news conferences.Osaka said players often faced repeated questions and comments that could create doubt. She did not want to keep putting herself through an experience she felt could harm her well-being.She also questioned the policy of forcing players to choose between media appearances and financial penalties. In the same statement, Osaka described the idea of telling athletes to “do press or be fined” while ignoring their mental health as “laughable.”Her request went beyond avoiding the penalty. Osaka expressed hope that the money she received as fines for skipping media duties would go to a mental health charity. That gave her protest a clear purpose: she wanted the issue to lead to support for people who needed it.However, the tournament authorities stood by their media requirements. On May 30, 2021, officials fined Osaka $15,000 for missing her post-match news conference after beating Patricia Maria Tig in the first round. The four Grand Slam tournaments then issued a joint statement warning that continued refusals could bring harsher penalties, including possible suspension from future events.Osaka withdrew from the French Open on May 31 rather than continue the dispute.In her withdrawal statement on May 31, Osaka explained that the situation had developed differently from what she expected. She wrote, “I never wanted to be a distraction.”She also spoke about her mental health struggles, revealing that she had experienced bouts of depression since the 2018 US Open and had dealt with social anxiety. Osaka said she would take time away from the court.Her announcement changed the conversation around the $15,000 fine. The dispute was no longer just about a player's obligation to speak to reporters. It also raised questions about how tennis could enforce media rules while recognising the personal pressures athletes face.Osaka’s proposed donation was an important part of that message. She wanted the money connected to the dispute to support mental health care rather than remain a punishment with no wider purpose. However, her stated wish to donate the fine money does not confirm that tournament officials ultimately gave it to a charity.The episode also highlighted a difficult balance in professional sport. Grand Slam organisers expect players to meet media obligations, while athletes must manage the demands of competition and public scrutiny. Osaka’s decision challenged tennis officials to consider how those responsibilities could coexist.Her withdrawal did not settle the debate, but it ensured that athlete mental health received attention beyond the court. By speaking openly about her struggles and asking for the fine money to support a mental health cause, Osaka turned a disciplinary dispute into a wider appeal for change.
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka wanted the French Open to take athletes' mental health more seriously. In May 2021, the tennis star announced that she would skip mandatory news conferences. She also hoped the fines for missing those appearances would support mental health charities. The French Open fined Osaka $15,000 on May 30, 2021, after she skipped a news conference following her first-round win.

Article Title: Sidney Crosby's $104.4 million contract changed his career finances, but the full story goes far beyond hockey
Article Text:
Sidney Crosby net worth 2026 (Image via Getty Images)

Sidney Crosby's $104.4 million deal set the foundation

Endorsements added another layer to his earnings

Why is Sidney Crosby's estimated net worth lower than his career earnings?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sidney Crosby’s career earnings reflect more than two decades of elite hockey and a long-standing relationship with the Pittsburgh Penguins. His 12-year, $104.4 million contract, signed in 2012, gave him long-term financial security and helped shape his standing among the NHL’s highest-paid players. Yet his estimated net worth is not simply a reflection of that deal. Endorsements, commercial partnerships and the distinction between salary earned and wealth accumulated all help explain his financial position. Crosby has built his reputation on the ice, but understanding his fortune requires looking beyond his contract.Crosby signed the contract in July 2012, committing to Pittsburgh for 12 years. The deal carried an average annual value of $8.7 million, a figure tied to his August 7 birthday and No. 87 jersey. It was a major commitment from the Penguins, but the investment paid off in ways that went beyond the team's books. Crosby helped Pittsburgh win Stanley Cup titles in 2016 and 2017, adding to the championship he had already secured in 2009.The contract also gave Crosby a degree of financial stability that few players enjoy across such a long stretch of their careers. He remained with one franchise, avoiding the uncertainty that often comes with changing teams and negotiating new deals.His earnings continued to grow, and in September 2024, he agreed to a two-year, $17.4 million extension that keeps him in Pittsburgh through the 2026-27 season.Crosby's income has never depended on hockey contracts alone. His reputation made him an attractive partner for brands looking to reach fans beyond the rink. Forbes reported in 2012 that he earned about $4 million annually from endorsements, including partnerships with Reebok, Tim Hortons, Bell Canada and Gatorade. The same report placed his total earnings at $12.7 million for that year, counting both his playing salary and commercial deals.That commercial appeal lasted well beyond his early years in the league. Crosby later worked with Adidas and other established brands, building a profile that reached consumers outside the core hockey audience. His marketability rested on more than trophies. He was a familiar face in a sport where star power can be harder to translate into mainstream recognition than in basketball or football.These deals help explain why his earning power has remained strong over time. They also show why a player's financial picture cannot be measured by his NHL contract alone. Endorsement income adds to gross earnings, though taxes, spending and other financial obligations affect how much of that money ultimately becomes personal wealth.Celebrity Net Worth estimates Crosby's fortune at $75 million, while its career earnings breakdown lists approximately $158.9 million in NHL salary. Those figures measure different things. Career earnings track money received over time, while net worth estimates what someone owns after accounting for liabilities. The two numbers should not be treated as interchangeable.The $75 million estimate is not a publicly audited account of Crosby's finances. His private investments, spending, taxes and other assets are not fully available for independent verification.That makes any precise claim about his wealth difficult to confirm, even when his contract history is well documented.Still, the broad picture is clear. Sidney Crosby has turned sustained success with Pittsburgh into more than $150 million in reported NHL salary earnings, backed by years of endorsement work. His 2012 contract was a defining part of that story, but it was not the whole story. The value of his name helped keep money flowing beyond the rink, even as the terms of his playing deals changed.
Article Summary: Sidney Crosby's 12-year, $104.4 million contract, signed in 2012, gave him long- term financial security. His estimated net worth is not simply a reflection of that deal. Endorsements, commercial partnerships and the distinction between salary earned and wealth accumulated all help explain his financial position.

But the hosts were stunned in the second match despite posting 249, as Shai Hope’s unbeaten century helped West Indies draw level in a record chase. Article Title: Home comfort, renewed confidence: Shubhankar Sharma, Anirban Lahiri target strong week at India Championship at DGC
Article Text:
Shubhankar Sharma

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shubhankar Sharma arrives at the India Championship with a win behind him at the recently concluded Kapil Dev Invitational in Greater Noida on Sunday and a renewed sense of belief. Anirban Lahiri, on the other hand, is hoping that time away from the game will help him return to his best. As the tournament begins at the Delhi Golf Club on Thursday, the two Indians will be looking to make the most of an important week on home soil.The $4 million championship has attracted a strong international field with the likes of Rory Mcllroy, Justin Rose, Aaron Rai and defending champion Tommy Fleetwood to name a few giving the Indian players an opportunity to test themselves against some of the best in the sport.For Sharma, the timing of his victory could prove significant. The two-time winner has endured a frustrating couple of seasons, with the effort he has put into his game not always translating into results.“My main goal of playing last week was to gain some momentum coming into this week. I wasn't thinking about winning,” Sharma said.He wanted to get back into a competitive routine, catch up with familiar faces and work out what needed to change in his game. The victory came as an unexpected bonus, but perhaps its biggest value was the confidence it restored.Sharma has also been making changes to his equipment and technique. After trying different clubs and finding it difficult to maintain consistency in varying conditions on the Tour, he decided to return to equipment he knew well. He has since made a few adjustments and worked on correcting habits that had begun to affect his performances.“The biggest victory was to see that the work that I'm putting in is now showing some result,” he said.What Sharma needs now is to produce his best golf more regularly and carry that form from one tournament to the next. Last week's result has given him reason to believe he is moving in the right direction.“The answer has always been very simple: I want to play with the best,” he said. “It's not about being comfortable for me. It's about being uncomfortable and conquering that feeling and going and performing.”Playing at Delhi Golf Club brings back memories of the early days of his golfing journey. As a young boy, Sharma watched international stars come to India and wondered whether he would ever get the chance to compete in a tournament of that standing at home.He remembers watching Ernie Els at a golf clinic in 2008, when he was around 12 years old. At the time, the prospect of sharing a tournament with leading international players seemed a long way off. Now, he is one of the home players hoping to make his presence felt in front of Indian fans.Sharma also has unfinished business at this championship. Last year, he produced an impressive second round but could not maintain that level over the remainder of the tournament. This time, he wants to build on that performance and avoid the fluctuations that have troubled him in the past.Meanwhile, Lahiri's preparations have been built around a different priority: taking a step back before returning to the demands of professional golf.The 39-year-old spent nearly seven weeks away from competition after a demanding stretch on the circuit. For the first three-and-a-half weeks, he barely touched his clubs, choosing instead to concentrate on his fitness and recovery. The decision followed an assessment with Dr Greg Rose at the Titleist Performance Institute, which helped shape his approach to getting his body back into better condition.Having spent two decades as a professional, Lahiri felt the need to devote more time to his physical well-being rather than continue pushing through a packed schedule.The break also gave him more time at home with his wife and two children, aged four and seven. With professional golf involving frequent travel and long periods away from family, the opportunity to slow down was welcome in its own right.Now back on the course, Lahiri says he feels ready for the challenge ahead.“I'm excited. I'm fresh. Mentally I'm in a really good space,” he said.His experience at Delhi Golf Club could be an advantage, although the course has changed since he last played there. Longer rough and firmer, recontoured greens have altered the test, making accuracy an important part of the equation.Lahiri believes the key will be to keep the ball in play and give himself manageable approaches to the greens. Players who stray from the fairways could find themselves struggling to create birdie chances, while those who strike their irons well should have opportunities to score.With so much quality in the field, Lahiri expects some low scores. But he also knows that players will have to be selective and patient, particularly on a course where one poor shot can undo the work of several good ones.The home setting adds another dimension to the week for both golfers. For Sharma, the tournament offers a chance to reconnect with friends and enjoy the familiarity of playing in India, something that can be difficult to find during a season spent travelling from one international event to another.Lahiri sees the championship as an opportunity to reconnect with the domestic game and help inspire younger golfers. Watching leading professionals compete alongside international stars can give aspiring players a clearer idea of what it takes to reach the highest level.Their routes into the tournament may have been different, but both Indians have reasons to approach the week with optimism.The real test begins on Thursday. A strong field will leave little room for lapses in concentration, and Delhi Golf Club is likely to reward those who combine accuracy with patience over all four rounds.For Sharma, the task is to turn a timely victory into sustained form. For Lahiri, it is to make his return count. With home support behind them, both will be hoping to give Indian golf something to celebrate.
Article Summary: Shubhankar Sharma and Anirban Lahiri are among the home players at the India Championship. Sharma won the Kapil Dev Invitational in Greater Noida on Sunday. Lahiri spent seven weeks away from the game after a demanding stretch on the circuit. The $4 million tournament begins at the Delhi Golf Club on Thursday.

Article Title: Ranji Trophy: Injury to Ayush Mhatre sours Mumbai’s win
Article Text:
Ayush Mhatre (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Mumbai’s emphatic start to the Ranji Trophy season has been hit by a major injury setback, with newly appointed vice-captain Ayush Mhatre ruled out for at least a month due to a recurrence of his right hamstring injury. The 19-year-old opener is set to miss Mumbai’s remaining three matches in the first phase of the Ranji Trophy after suffering the injury during his 48-run knock on Day One of the opener against Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium.Mumbai won the match by an innings and 155 runs on Tuesday, collecting a bonus point, but Mhatre’s injury took the sheen off the result. “Ayush has suffered a Grade 4 tear of his right hamstring. He should be out for at least one to one-and-a-half months,” a source in the Mumbai Cricket Association told TOI on Tuesday.A medical expert, however, said a Grade 4 hamstring tear usually indicates a severe injury. “If it’s a Grade 4 hamstring tear, it usually requires surgery. He could be out for nothing less than four to six months,” the expert told this paper.The recurrence of Mhatre’s injury has again brought into focus the role of the medical team at BCCI’s Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, where he had undergone rehabilitation for injuries to both his left and right hamstrings for almost three months.He had been ruled out of action since the second half of the IPL while playing for Chennai Super Kings.The injury is a significant setback for Mhatre, who had only recently been named Siddhesh Lad ’s deputy for the Ranji Trophy by the Mumbai selectors. The top-order batter had earlier suffered a left hamstring injury while playing for CSK, which kept him out for nearly five months. He missed the T20 Mumbai tournament in June, the India A tour to Sri Lanka and the Duleep Trophy in August. A subsequent right hamstring injury further delayed his comeback.After sustaining the latest injury, Mhatre did not take the field on Days Two and Three of the Ranji opener. He underwent scans on Monday, with substitute Suved Parkar fielding in his place.“It’s unfortunate because he had just returned from another hamstring injury. He looks very sad. He worked very hard during rehab. He was doing rehab with me only at MCA-BKC. He used to come from Virar just to do his rehab and then go back,” Mumbai captain Siddhesh Lad told reporters after Mumbai’s win.“So, it happens. It’s part of the game. But we will try to motivate him. It seems he will not be with the team for some time now. The way he was limping in the match, it does not look like he will be available for the second or third match,” Lad added.Lad said the injury occurred while Mhatre was running between the wickets. “We had two or three simulations and club games, and also played at BKC. He was looking fine for the last three-four matches, but all of a sudden, he felt something in his hamstring while taking a second run,” Lad said.At the pre-season news conference, Mhatre had spoken about his long injury layoff and preparation for the season. “I was at the CoE for three months. The preparation is going really well,” he had said.When he first suffered the injury on April 18 during CSK’s match against Sunrisers Hyderabad, Mhatre was CSK’s leading run-scorer in the tournament, with 201 runs in six innings at a strike rate of 177.87.Brief Scores: Mumbai 429 bt Chandigarh 78 &196 (Bhambri 44; Mulani 3-69, Kotian 3-30, Deshpande 2-37) by an innings and 155 runs.
Article Summary: Ayush Mhatre ruled out for at least a month due to a recurrence of his right hamstring injury. The 19-year-old opener is set to miss Mumbai’s remaining three matches in the first phase of the Ranji Trophy. Mumbai won the match by an innings and 155 runs on Tuesday, collecting a bonus point.

Article Title: Drama! Qais Ahmed's injury moment brings back memories of Gulbadin Naib's T20 World Cup incident
Article Text:
Qais Ahmed and Gulbadin Naib (Image credit: Agencies)

Qais Ahmed's injury moment in the final overs

Sediqullah Atal scores maiden Test century

Gulbadin Naib's injury incident at T20 World Cup 2024

NEW DELHI: Qais Ahmed grabbed attention in the closing stages of the one-off Test between Afghanistan and Bangladesh in Abu Dhabi. The Afghanistan batter's injury moment reminded fans of Gulbadin Naib's incident during the 2024 T20 World Cup. Afghanistan put up a determined batting effort to secure a draw at the Sheikh Zayed Stadium. The hosts batted for 142 overs to avoid defeat against their Asian rivals.Qais played an important role in ensuring that the efforts of Afghanistan's batters, especially Sediqullah Atal, did not go in vain. Batting at number nine, he remained unbeaten on 49 off 80 balls and helped his team survive the final stages of the match.With just 10 minutes left in the match, Qais blocked a delivery from Taijul Islam in the third-last over before going down while holding his left hamstring.The moment caught the attention of social media users, while Bangladesh players appeared pleased with the situation.The incident reminded fans of Naib's injury moment against Bangladesh during the 2024 T20 World Cup. Afghanistan won that match to reach the semi-finals of an ICC tournament for the first time.Qais made another important contribution in the final over, hitting two sixes as Afghanistan and Bangladesh settled for a draw.Atal played a key role in Afghanistan's effort to save the Test. He scored 111 off 333 balls to register the first Test century of his career. He also became the first Afghanistan batter to score a century in the fourth innings of a Test match.Captain Rahmat Shah also had a memorable game. In his first Test as captain, he scored 105 in the first innings and followed it up with 51 in the second. Rahmat became only the sixth male cricketer to score a century and a half-century on his Test captaincy debut.Afghanistan created history at the 2024 T20 World Cup by beating Bangladesh to reach the semi-finals of an ICC tournament for the first time. However, the match also drew attention because of an incident involving Naib.During the 12th over of Bangladesh's innings, Naib went down holding his hamstring shortly after head coach Jonathan Trott was seen signalling to the players to slow the game down. At that stage, Afghanistan were two runs ahead under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method, with the match finely balanced.Naib's injury led to the physios coming onto the field. Play was then stopped as rain interrupted the match. When the teams returned after a short break, Naib appeared to be moving comfortably. This led to criticism from some fans and experts, who questioned the timing of the incident and suggested it may have helped Afghanistan.Afghanistan eventually defeated Najmul Hossain Shanto's Bangladesh by eight runs under the DLS method. The result also knocked Australia out of the race for a semi-final spot.
Article Summary: Qais Ahmed grabbed attention in the closing stages of the one-off Test between Afghanistan and Bangladesh in Abu Dhabi. The Afghanistan batter's injury moment reminded fans of Gulbadin Naib's incident during the 2024 T20 World Cup. Afghanistan put up a determined batting effort to secure a draw at the Sheikh Zayed Stadium.

BHOPAL: After spending eight months cleaning the Ajnar River in Madhya Pradesh, environmental activist and content creator Bittu Tabahi has returned to find garbage dumped along its banks again.In an Instagram video, Bittu expressed disappointment over the river’s condition and showed himself removing waste once more, prompting social media users to question the lack of civic sense and praise his continued efforts."I never imagined that eight months of my hard work would go to waste like this," Bittu wrote as the caption of the video shared on Instagram.Bittu explained that he carries his own equipment and wears gloves before beginning the cleanup to protect himself. In September, he and his team collected 585kg of waste from a stretch of the Yamuna in Delhi before moving to Gurugram’s Khedki Daula, where they removed 2,435kg of waste.The drive was part of a three-city cleanup campaign that also included Noida.His work on the Ajnar River had earlier drawn attention for the scale of the cleanup and his efforts to remove garbage without sophisticated equipment.The latest video highlights the challenge of sustaining such efforts when waste continues to accumulate at previously cleaned sites.
