NEW DELHI: The selection committee is likely to leave it as late as possible before naming the ODI and Test teams for the upcoming tour of New Zealand as they wait on the fitness status of Prasidh Krishna, Harshit Rana and Rishabh Pant.TOI understands that Krishna has been given a three-week timeline when he reported to the Centre of Excellence (CoE) after he walked out of the second ODI against West Indies in Guwahati on Sept 30. Seam-bowling allrounder Rana, who has been at the CoE since July, is expected to undergo a return-to-play match simulation on October 25 before the ODI and Test squads are expected to fly out on October 28 with the ODI series scheduled to start on Nov 4. BCCI , on Monday, announced that Pant will not be available for the first two India ‘A’ four-day matches starting on Oct 24 due to a side strain he picked up in the Irani Cup match. It is learnt that the CoE has adopted a cautious approach in clearing players after rehab.Sources told TOI that the Indian team management had pulled out Krishna after bowling five overs in Guwahati as a precautionary measure after he complained of some discomfort in his left hamstring.“With both Pant and Krishna, the injuries don’t look severe at the outset. But the CoE doesn’t want to take any chances. That’s why both of them were given threeweek timelines when they reported to CoE,” a BCCI source told TOI.“The selectors and team management are keen to have Rana in both formats, and he is seen as a perfect fit as the seam-bowling allrounder batting at No. 8,” the source added.Krishna is seen as a primary member of the pacebowling attack in both Tests and ODIs while Pant will form the batting mainstay during the two-Test series starting on Nov 19. Pant had asked for game time with the India ‘A’ team to find rhythm before the Tests.The Test team is expected to play a warm-up match before the first Test after the third India ‘A’ four-day match finishes on Nov 10.It has also emerged that Bhuvneshwar Kumar, who has been picked for the T20Is after four years, is undergoing training at the CoE. Over the last three years, the 36-yearold had designed his calendar to prepare for the IPL. He has only been playing T20s in domestic cricket. The camp at CoE is intended to get back in shape for the rigours international cricket.
Article Summary: The selection committee is likely to leave it as late as possible before naming the ODI and Test teams for the upcoming tour of New Zealand. Prasidh Krishna has been given a three-week timeline when he reported to the Centre of Excellence (CoE) after he walked out of the second ODI against West Indies in Guwahati. Seam-bowling allrounder Harshit Rana is expected to undergo a return-to-play match simulation on October 25.

Article Title: Scientists discover ‘hidden materials’ that may lead to better batteries and solar fuels
Article Text:
Representational image

Why this discovery is important

Uncovering 'new form' of Bismuth Vanadate

Promising breakthrough for next-generation batteries

An international research team has uncovered a class of previously unknown “hidden materials” by tracking the elusive, split-second changes that occur as molecules decompose under heat. The findings, published in Nature Communications, may unlock new pathways to develop more efficient solar fuel systems and higher-capacity batteries.Typically, when materials scientists create solid compounds through thermal processing, attention is paid almost entirely to the final outcome – which is essentially moving straight from starting material “A” to end product “B.” However, by freezing and analysing the fleeting intermediate phases that arise during the heating cycle, researchers discovered entirely new structures that are difficult or impossible to manufacture using standard synthesis methods.“When materials are made by heating, scientists usually focus on the final product, the 'B' that results from 'A.' But this study shows that there are many fascinating stages in between 'A' and 'B,' and these hidden steps could be just as important,” said Dr. Sebastian Pike from the Department of Chemistry at the University of Warwick.“We didn't know exactly what we would find going in, but we were confident there would be something interesting and unknown in the intermediate phases.We were thrilled to discover that some of these could have practical uses, even from the very first experiments,” Pike added.The team began their experiments using customised “single-source precursors” – single molecules engineered to contain every fundamental element required to yield a targeted solid material. As temperatures steadily rose, the scientists monitored how the molecular bonds broke apart and reassembled. This tracking exposed several uncharted material phases, most notably a newly discovered, kinetically stabilized form of bismuth vanadate.Standard bismuth vanadate has been prized in renewable energy engineering due to its optimal “band gap” – the exact energy threshold needed to absorb sunlight and catalyze chemical reactions. This characteristic allows it to harvest solar energy efficiently while providing the required chemical punch to split water molecules into clean hydrogen fuel.The newly identified ‘form’ features a distinct atomic architecture that sets it apart from all previously cataloged variations of the compound. Crucially, it possesses a significantly wider band gap, fundamentally changing how the material absorbs and reacts to light. Researchers note that this shift introduces fresh avenues to fine-tune materials across catalysis, advanced electronics, and solar fuel generation.The utility of these intermediate materials extends beyond solar energy. During the testing process, the scientists isolated another transient phase exhibiting high-capacity lithium storage, suggesting immediate promise for next-generation battery architectures.“What's exciting is that these 'in-between' materials aren't just stepping stones — they can have useful properties in their own right,” explained Dr. Dominik Kubicki from the School of Chemistry at the University of Birmingham. “By understanding and controlling how they form, we can start to design better materials for batteries, catalysis, and solar energy.”
Article Summary: University of Warwick researchers have discovered a class of previously unknown 'hidden materials' by tracking the elusive, split-second changes that occur as molecules decompose under heat. The findings may unlock new pathways to develop more efficient solar fuel systems and higher-capacity batteries.

Article Title: BFI suspends secretary general Pramod Kumar over alleged financial irregularities
Article Text:
BFI president Ajay Singh and Pramod Kumar

Suspension follows Kumar's letter to PM Modi

Inquiry into cancellation of national championship

Dispute over no-confidence motion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kumar barred from performing secretary general's duties

The Boxing Federation of India (BFI) has suspended its secretary general Pramod Kumar with immediate effect over alleged financial irregularities, failure to cooperate with investigations and misuse of authority. BFI president Ajay Singh issued the suspension order on Tuesday, pending an inquiry into the allegations against Kumar. These include issuing a work order for broadcasting arrangements without the required approval.Kumar has also been accused of not cooperating with an inquiry into the cancellation of a national championship and trying to call an unauthorised meeting to move a no-confidence motion against Singh."You are hereby placed under interim suspension from the office of Secretary General with immediate effect, pending completion of the inquiry or until the order is modified or revoked by the competent authority, subject to the applicable provisions of the BFI Constitution," read the order, in possession of PTI.The order clarified that the suspension was temporary and "shall not be construed as a final determination of the allegations".The action came a day after Kumar wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, accusing Singh and BFI Executive Director Col. Arun Malik of "criminal intimidation" to stop the proposed no-confidence motion. Malik dismissed the allegation as "baseless".One of the main issues raised in the suspension order concerns a claim by Pinnacle Broadcast Productions for around Rs 1.5 crore for broadcasting services at the World Boxing Finals Cup in Greater Noida in November 2025.In an earlier letter to the BFI president, Kumar had said Pinnacle had committed Rs 2 crore towards sponsorship and broadcasting for the event. However, the company has denied making such a commitment."The Federation has recently received notices from Pinnacle Broadcast Productions making a claim for Rs. 1.5 crore (approx.) for broadcasting undertaken in the World Boxing Final's Cup, Greater Noida, November 2025."Whereas, the understanding as per the letter forwarded by you to the President was that Pinnacle had committed and assured Rs. 2 crore for the sponsorship and broadcasting of the event.""Pinnacle has now categorically denied making any such commitment, which raises serious doubt as to the authenticity of the letter that you personally represented Pinnacle had issued."The order also alleged that Kumar had signed a work order without getting approval from the federation's finance committee.Singh also referred to an inquiry into the last-minute cancellation of the BFI Elite Men and Women Open Boxing Championship. The event was scheduled to take place in Nahan, Himachal Pradesh, from August 16 to 23.An inquiry committee was formed on August 17 to investigate the cancellation. However, according to the suspension order, Kumar repeatedly sought more time and did not answer the committee's questions."...you have been repeatedly seeking time and have failed to respond to the notice issued to you and the specific questions raised by the duly constituted Inquiry Committee."Another reason cited for Kumar's suspension was his alleged attempt to issue notices against senior federation officials and call a meeting to move a no-confidence motion against Singh.Last week, Kumar called for a Special General Meeting (SGM) on October 28. He claimed that he had the support of a majority of affiliated state units to move the motion against the BFI president."It is deeply concerning that, instead of cooperating with the ongoing investigations, you have purported to issue cease-and-desist notices against senior officials of the BFI, show cause notices and a notice purporting to convene a meeting to move a no confidence motion against the President," the order read.The order stated that Kumar did not have the authority under the BFI Constitution to issue such notices without the required approval or call special general meetings on his own.It also accused him of sending communications to federation officials and staff asking them to ignore the president's authority and claiming control of the BFI administration."You have also issued communications to the officials and staff of BFI instigating them to disregard the authority of the President of the BFI and claiming to be at the helm of the administration of the BFI."Under the suspension order, Kumar has been directed not to perform his duties as secretary general, send communications on behalf of the federation or access official records related to the inquiry.The order also warned of further disciplinary action if he attempts to violate the suspension, obstruct the investigation, misuse the federation's authority or interfere with the proceedings."Any attempt to violate the instant order of suspension, obstruct the inquiry, misuse the authority of BFI or interfere with its proceedings shall be viewed seriously and may invite further disciplinary action in accordance with the BFI Constitution and applicable rules and regulations."
Article Summary: Boxing Federation of India suspends secretary general Pramod Kumar with immediate effect. Kumar accused of financial irregularities, failure to cooperate with investigations and misuse of authority. BFI president Ajay Singh issued the suspension order on Tuesday, pending an inquiry into the allegations against Kumar. Kumar also accused of not cooperating with inquiry into cancellation of national championship.

Article Title: 'King Charles III's affection for India is well-known'
Article Text:
(L-R) Lindy Cameron, Dr Jitendra Singh, Jonathan Reynolds

Chef Vineet Bhatia with Angela Eagle, Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs of the UK

I will miss India tremendously: Lindy Cameron

(L-R) Thierry Mathou, French ambassador, Oleksandr Polishchuk, Ukrainian ambassador, Jasper Wieck, German ambassador

‘There’s a natural gravitational pull between UK & India’

Ben Mellor, deputy High Commissioner with Lindy Cameron

I met my wife in Delhi: Ben Mellor

(L-R) Xu Feihong, Chinese ambassador, Diana Mickevičienė, Lithuanian ambassador, Antonio Bartoli, Italian ambassador

(L-R) Dr Anupam Sibal, Sara Abdullah, Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh, Palestinian ambassador

(L-R) Douglas Alexander, Secretary of State for Scotland, Stefan Priesner, United Nations Resident Coordinator in India, Kim McGuiness, Mayor of North East England

DJ Nida Merchant





On a cool October evening, the British High Commissioner threw a party for King Charles III’s birthday for the diplomatic circle in the city. With Navratri bites, a live food counter, and music, the evening was complete with a dance floor to wrap up the festivities. It also marked the final event hosted by current High Commissioner Lindy Cameron before she heads back to the UK. A delegation of UK cabinet ministers and mayors was also in attendance.Reflecting the fusion of the two cultures, the menu featured pairings such as vanilla ice cream with gulkand, Dal pakwan shortbread, and British potato salad. Guests also enjoyed a spread of canapes and sweet treats. Adding to the evening’s culinary highlights was a live cooking experience by chef Vineet Bhatia.Starting with a warm ‘Namaste doston’, Lindy Cameron addressed the gathering, “Tonight is a celebration of His Majesty the King, of friendship, and of a very bright future for UK-India partnership. As our landmark economic and trade agreement entered into force, I am proud that you can see that future in action. As we celebrate His Majesty King Charles’ birthday and our national day, we also celebrate a future full of opportunity.” She added, “I wish I could be here to see that partnership grow further, but after two and a half fabulous years in India, I’ll be returning to the UK shortly to become the new permanent undersecretary of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. I will miss you all and India tremendously, more than I can tell you.”Dr Jitendra Singh, Minister for Science, Technology and Earth Sciences, who was the chief guest of the event, said, “It’s a privilege to be here on the national day and to celebrate the birthday of His Majesty. Our countries have a legacy which shares common cultural ties. When we have a bonhomie and a natural bond happening, everything becomes easier, even doing business. Our relationship has grown by leaps and bounds over the last decade because India has been able to elicit confidence in stability in fellow nations. And the bond existing between the UK and India has also strengthened in more ways than one. It goes beyond the trade matrix.”Referring to the UK-India Trade Deal which was brought into effect in July of this year, Jonathan Reynolds, UK Business and Trade Secretary, said, “There’s a natural gravitational pull between the UK and India. And His Majesty The King has played his own part in nurturing that relationship. Throughout his public life, the King has been an extraordinary ambassador for the United Kingdom overseas. His affection for India is well-known, and across ten official visits, he has built his own deep and enduring relationship with this country. ”As Lindy Cameron departs India, Ben Mellor, deputy High Commissioner, will be taking over as the interim High Commissioner. Speaking to us at the reception, he said, “I actually first lived here about 25 years ago. I was here for four years; it’s actually where I met my wife. Delhi has changed in all those years; it’s a whole different place, but it’s lovely to be back. We’re really happy to be meeting old friends and making new ones. It’s a fantastic place to celebrate the King’s birthday. His Majesty is a massive fan of India and of the UK-India relationship. The only thing better than celebrating his birthday here would be if he were able to come to India himself to celebrate. It’s an honour to be a small part of his celebration.”
Article Summary: The British High Commissioner threw a party for King Charles III’s birthday for the diplomatic circle in the city. With Navratri bites, a live food counter, and music, the evening was complete with a dance floor. It also marked the final event hosted by current High Commissioner Lindy Cameron before she heads back to the UK.

Article Title: 4 injured as tanker rams BEST bus at Mumbai’s Cheda Nagar Junction
Article Text:
An accident involving a tanker and a BEST wet-lease bus at Cheda Nagar Junction in Mumbai left four passengers injured





MUMBAI: Four passengers were injured after a tanker rammed into a BEST wet-lease bus at Cheda Nagar Junction in Mumbai on Wednesday morning, shattering three windowpanes and leaving passengers hurt by broken glass.The incident occurred around 6.55am on October 14, when the bus (MH-03-CV-7035), operating on route A-373/32 from Vaishali Nagar to Mahul, stopped at a traffic signal after a motorcycle suddenly came in front of it. A tanker travelling from Mumbai towards Vashi then crashed into the middle portion of the bus’s right side.The impact shattered three windowpanes, injuring four passengers. Bhagyashree Khedkar, 14, sustained an injury below her right eye, while Aditi Koyande, 22, suffered bleeding injuries to her right elbow and leg.The bus conductor took the two women to Rajawadi Hospital for treatment. One male passenger who sustained minor injuries refused medical treatment, while another injured passenger was taken to a hospital by relatives.Police took both vehicles to Tilak Nagar police station for further action.
Article Summary: tanker rammed into a BEST wet-lease bus at Cheda Nagar Junction in Mumbai on Wednesday morning. The impact shattered three windowpanes, injuring four passengers. Bhagyashree Khedkar, 14, sustained an injury below her right eye. Aditi Koyande, 22, suffered bleeding injuries to her right elbow and leg.

Article Title: Barricade row sparks temple fracas as devotees fume over Mahalaxmi Navaratra arrangements
Article Text:
A heated arguement broke out between the Shripujaks, Paschim Maharashtra Devasthan Samiti and the police at Mahalaxmi temple on Monday, the second day of Navratra

Kolhapur

:





A row over crowd management at Kolhapur’s Mahalaxmi temple erupted into a public fracas on Monday, with priests, temple authorities and police clashing over barricading and movement restrictions that devotees say have turned a revered pilgrimage into an ordeal.The confrontation broke out on the second day of Navaratra when Shripujaks (priests) accused the administration of interfering in religious practices and insulting them by obstructing temple rituals. The protest inside the temple premises briefly disrupted the otherwise festive atmosphere.Since Navaratra began, devotees and priests have been voicing anger over altered entry and exit routes and extensive barricading put in place by police. Instead of easing movement, the measures have triggered confusion, longer queues and growing resentment among devotees.“The Mukhdarshan route, which was convenient every year, has been made complicated this Navaratra. The waiting time, which earlier used to be around 15 to 20 minutes, has increased to nearly an hour,” said devotee Smita Patil from Mangalwar Peth.Devotees also complained about poor facilities along the queues.Patil said there was no matting on parts of the Pradakshina route, forcing devotees to walk on hot surfaces, while shade arrangements on the Mukhdarshan queue were inadequate.Tempers flared further on Monday afternoon when members of Hindu outfits objected to barricades erected inside the temple precincts. Heated arguments followed as protesters questioned the need for the restrictions and accused authorities of making darshan unnecessarily difficult.“The administration claims there is coordination between the authorities, the Devasthan Samiti and the police, but it has forgotten the connection between devotees and the goddess. Lakhs of devotees visit the Mahalaxmi temple every year with deep faith. This time, the barricading makes the temple premises look like an international border, with devotees being treated like terrorists,” a protester said.The protesters warned that if the barricades were not removed, they would take matters into their own hands and dismantle them from Tuesday. The episode exposed growing cracks in coordination between Paschim Maharashtra Devasthan Samiti, police and temple stakeholders at a time when lakhs of devotees are expected during the nine-day festival.Despite the controversy, the flow of devotees remained unabated. Temple authorities recorded 1,19,205 devotees on Monday alone.The goddess was adorned in the revered Sarvasyada Mahalaxmi form, with ritual worship performed by priests Ajinkya Munishwar, Vedang Munishwar, Soham Munishwar and Ravi Mainkar. But outside the sanctum, the focus remained firmly on the crowd-control measures that turned a day of devotion into a day of confrontation.
Article Summary: Priests, authorities and police clash at Mahalaxmi temple on second day of Navaratra. Shripujaks (priests) accuse administration of interfering in religious practices. Protesters question need for restrictions and accuse authorities of making darshan unnecessarily difficult.

Article Title: 3 devotees die in 2 accidents
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





Three devotees died in two separate accidents while carrying a flambeau (jyot) from Tuljapur to their villages.Sambhaji Prahlad Kadam (40) and Rajesh Appasaheb Kadam (38) were among a group of 17 people from Kouthali village in Atpadi taluka of Sangli district, who had travelled to Tuljapur to bring the jyot. The flame is kept burning at their village pandal throughout the nine days of Navaratra.On Sunday morning, while returning along Tuljapur-Dharashiv Road at Tuljainagar, a goods carrier vehicle hit the two-wheeler they were riding on. They were rushed to hospital, but were declared brought dead. Other devotees returned to the village with their bodies.In the second case, 45-year-old Prakash Jagganath Dighe from Wadegaon in Sangola taluka of Solapur district was run over by an unknown vehicle. The accident took place around 4.30 pm on Sunday along Sangola-Mangalwedha road.During Navaratra, devotees traditionally bring a flame from Shaktipeeths, such as Mahalaxmi in Kolhapur, where the goddess is the main deity. They leave days before the festival begins and carry the flame while running barefoot, exchanging it after covering a certain distance.Other participants follow on motorbikes and in a carrier vehicle, cooking and eating along the roadside during the journey.
Article Summary: Sambhaji Prahlad Kadam, Rajesh Appasaheb Kadam and Prakash Jagganath Dighe died. They were among 17 people who had travelled to Tuljapur to bring the jyot. The flame is kept burning at their village pandal throughout Navaratra.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.

Article Title: GMRT detects hydrogen signal from galaxies 8 billion years ago
Article Text:
The GMRT, near Pune, was designed nearly four decades ago to detect the hydrogen signal from galaxies in the early Universe

Pune:





Indian astronomers, using the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT) near Pune, recently detected an extremely faint radio signal of atomic hydrogen from galaxies that existed 8-9 billion years ago. The detection is a step towards understanding how stars formed in the early Universe and why star formation has declined over billions of years.Atomic hydrogen is the basic fuel galaxies need to make stars. It combines to form molecular hydrogen, from which stars are formed. Measuring how much atomic hydrogen galaxies contain at different stages of the Universe’s history helps astronomers understand how galaxies grow and why their star formation has slowed. It’s widely believed that star formation has fallen, the peak being 10 billion years ago. It’s estimated that about half of the stellar mass today had already formed by roughly 9 billion years ago.The Indian team that made the recent detection said their findings, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, suggest although galaxies in the early Universe had larger reserves of atomic hydrogen, they were also forming stars at a much faster rate than galaxies today.This essentially means they consumed their gas quickly. And without fresh supplies of gas from their surroundings, these galaxies eventually ran short of the material needed to form new stars, members of the team said.The research was carried out by experts from the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics (NCRA-TIFR) and the Inter-University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics (IUCAA). They combined signals from nearly 10,000 distant galaxies to measure their average atomic hydrogen content.“We used the GMRT to look at a region in the sky called the COSMOS field for more than 200 hours. We aligned the ‘HI 21 cm’ signals of nearly 10,000 galaxies and then averaged them together to measure the average atomic hydrogen content of the galaxies,” said Balpreet Kaur, lead author of the study and a postdoctoral fellow at IUCAA.The HI 21 cm signal is emitted by atomic hydrogen at a radio wavelength of about 21cm. Radio telescopes can detect this signal and help scientists estimate the amount of hydrogen in galaxies. Since light and radio signals from distant galaxies take billions of years to reach Earth, astronomers observe these galaxies as they existed in the distant past.Kaur said the team’s findings, indicating galaxies run out of star-forming fuel, provide a “natural explanation for the observed drop in the star-formation activity of the universe over the last 8 billion years”.Co-author Aditya Chowdhury said the method helped overcome a major challenge in studying the early universe. “The HI 21 cm signal is so faint that it is extremely challenging to detect it from individual galaxies that existed at these early times. However, the ‘HI 21 cm stacking’ technique combines the signals of many galaxies and allows us to measure their average signal,” said Chowdhury, who completed his PhD at NCRA-TIFR.Co-author Jayaram N Chengalur said the COSMOS field was particularly useful because astronomers already had extensive information about its galaxies from observations made using different types of light. Researchers can now compare their hydrogen content with other properties, including their surroundings, to better understand how galaxies evolve.Nissim Kanekar, another co-author and faculty member at NCRA-TIFR, said the detection was an important step towards measuring the hydrogen signal from individual galaxies from that period — something astronomers have not yet achieved. The team is carrying out deeper observations of the same region using the GMRT in an attempt to reach that goal.
Article Summary: Astronomers using the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT) near Pune, recently detected an extremely faint radio signal of atomic hydrogen from galaxies that existed 8-9 billion years ago. The detection is a step towards understanding how stars formed in the early Universe and why star formation has declined over billions of years.

Article Title: ‘When Justice Bose waited at police station without revealing he was HC judge’
Article Text:
Justice Anil Kilor delivered a lecture on ‘The Legacy of the Bar Association and the Role of Junior Lawyers’, organised by HCBA, on Tuesday





Nagpur: Justice Vivian Bose, despite being a high court judge, once quietly sat on a bench outside a police station after being asked to accompany the police, without revealing his identity or expressing displeasure, recalled Justice Anil Kilor while highlighting the importance of humility and simplicity in professional and personal life.Sharing the anecdote during a lecture on ‘The Legacy of the Bar Association and the Role of Junior Lawyers’, organised by HCBA here on Tuesday, the senior administrative judge said the incident had been narrated to him by former Chief Justice of India Sharad Bobde, when he was working with him.“Justice Bose owned a Fiat car and frequently travelled to Pachmarhi. On one such journey, the police stopped his car and asked him to accompany them to the police station,” the judge said.Without disclosing he was an HC judge, Bose complied, without expressing displeasure or asserting his position. After some time, a senior police officer recognised Justice Bose and apologised for the conduct of his staff.Justice Kilor said the incident conveyed an important lesson: even after achieving great heights in life, people should retain simplicity in their thinking, lifestyle and approach towards others.Recalling his initial struggles with legal concepts, Justice Kilor recalled feeling insecure after a friend explained legal concepts that he struggled to understand. “However, over time, I realised that young practitioners need not possess exhaustive knowledge at the outset of their careers. What matters is their willingness to learn and readiness to work hard,” he said.“Ex-CJI Bobde, during his time as a lawyer, told me that even if you feel a judge is hostile towards you, appear before him,” Kilor said, adding that Bobde advised preparing thrice as much during such scenarios. “He explained that when a judge repeatedly sees the quality of preparation and your determination to pursue justice, his attitude may eventually change,” Kilor said.Addressing young lawyers, Justice Kilor said they might go on to become senior advocates, judges or occupy other distinguished positions. However, they should never forget the importance of humility and simplicity, irrespective of the heights they achieve.
Article Summary: Justice Vivian Bose sat on a bench outside a police station after being asked to accompany the police, without revealing his identity or expressing displeasure. Justice Anil Kilor shared the anecdote during a lecture on ‘The Legacy of the Bar Association and the Role of Junior Lawyers’

Article Title: Man gets 10-year rigorous imprisonment for raping minor on pretext of marriage
Article Text:
Nashik

:





A Nashik District and Sessions Court on Monday sentenced a man to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment (RI) for repeatedly sexually assaulting a minor girl, resulting in her pregnancy. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 3,000 and ordered him to pay Rs 1 lakh in compensation to the survivor.The accused and the survivor had known each other for a long time. He repeatedly sexually assaulted her at different places in the city. The survivor was just over 15 years old when she lodged a complaint with Mumbai Naka police.Police registered a case under relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. PSI Pankaj Sonawane, then attached to Mumbai Naka police station, gathered circumstantial and forensic evidence before filing a chargesheet.Based on the survivor’s testimony, witness statements and evidence presented by the investigating officer, District and Sessions Judge R N Pandhare found the accused guilty under relevant sections of the POCSO Act The court said failure to pay the fine would attract an additional three months of RI.It also directed the convict to pay Rs 1 lakh in compensation to the survivor within a month, failing which he would face an additional year of RI.APP Bhanupriya Petkar represented the govt during the trial.Nashik CP Sandeep Karnik, DCP Kirankumar Chavan, DCP Monika Raut and other senior officials commended the prosecution team and police personnel for securing the conviction.
Article Summary: A Nashik District and Sessions Court on Monday sentenced a man to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment (RI) for repeatedly sexually assaulting a minor girl, resulting in her pregnancy. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 3,000 and ordered him to pay Rs 1 lakh in compensation to the survivor.

Article Title: Kevin Wickham earns maiden Test call-up for West Indies' Bangladesh tour

Kevin Wickham (Image credit: Cricket West Indies)

Wickham rewarded for strong domestic performances

West Indies to arrive in Bangladesh on October 18

West Indies Test squad for Bangladesh tour

Top-order batter Kevin Wickham has received his first call-up to the West Indies Test team for the upcoming two-match series in Bangladesh. The 15-member squad will play its final series of the 2025-2027 ICC World Test Championship cycle.The first Test will begin on October 28 in Mirpur, while the second match will start on November 5 in Sylhet.White-ball captain Shai Hope has been rested for the series after playing across all three formats for an extended period. He is currently leading the West Indies in their white-ball series against India.The 23-year-old Wickham has earned his maiden senior-level Test call-up after an impressive run in the West Indies Championship.He scored three consecutive centuries in the competition, with his highest score being 153. Wickham has now hit six centuries in 25 first-class matches at an average of over 40.Fast bowler Alzarri Joseph has been withdrawn from the squad led by Roston Chase following a routine medical assessment and consultation with specialists.Cricket West Indies (CWI) has decided to manage Joseph's workload to reduce the risk of injury because of the increased physical demands of red-ball cricket.Joseph will continue to work with the CWI medical team and specialists as he prepares to return to the longer format.All-rounder Keemo Paul has been named as Joseph's replacement for the Bangladesh series.Opener John Campbell is back in the squad after recovering from a hamstring injury. The injury had ruled him out of the home series against Pakistan.The rest of the squad remains the same as the group that beat Sri Lanka and drew its series against Pakistan during the summer.Hope has been rested as the West Indies manage his workload ahead of the ICC Cricket World Cup Qualifier, scheduled for February next year.West Indies head coach Daren Sammy said the team wants to improve its position in the World Test Championship standings by winning the Bangladesh series."At the start of this World Test Championship cycle we set ourselves goals, and one of them was to finish in the top half of the rankings."Winning this series would move us closer to it. Playing Bangladesh in their own conditions will be challenging, and we're ready for that," head coach Daren Sammy said in a CWI statement.A series victory could help the West Indies climb to sixth in the ICC Test rankings at the end of the current cycle. The team finished the 2023-2025 cycle in eighth place.The full West Indies squad will reach Bangladesh on October 18. The visitors will then play a three-day warm-up match in Dhaka from October 22 to 24 before the Test series begins.Roston Chase (C), Jomel Warrican (VC), Joshua Bishop, John Campbell, Tagenarine Chanderpaul, Joshua Da Silva, Justin Greaves, Kavem Hodge, Amir Jangoo, Shamar Joseph, Brandon King, Keemo Paul, Kemar Roach, Jayden Seales, Kevin Wickham.
Article Summary: West Indies to arrive in Bangladesh on October 18. First Test will begin on October 28 in Mirpur. Second match will start on November 5 in Sylhet. Wickham rewarded for strong domestic performances. Alzarri Joseph ruled out, Keemo Paul replaces him. John Campbell returns to the squad.

Article Title: Parthiv Patel takes entrepreneurial route, targets AI-driven cricket development
Article Text:
Former India cricketer Parthiv Patel has ventured into entrepreneurship with an AI-based platform aimed at improving player development and talent identification in cricket.

Former India cricketer Parthiv Patel has ventured into entrepreneurship, with a focus on using artificial intelligence to improve player development and talent identification in cricket.Patel, who has worked with Mumbai Indians and Gujarat Titans in talent scouting and coaching after his playing career, has teamed up with entrepreneurs Kunal Abhishek and Shamik Datta for the venture.The initiative aims to make performance analysis more accessible to cricketers, particularly those at the grassroots level who may not have access to specialist coaches, analysts and video technology.Its first application offers video analysis, personalised feedback and performance tracking to help players identify areas for improvement."Throughout my career, I've seen how much of cricket still depends on fragmented information and individual observation," Patel said, highlighting the limitations of relying solely on individual assessments to identify and develop talent.He added that artificial intelligence could help make cricketing insights more accessible to young players, regardless of where they train or the resources available to them.Patel, however, stressed that technology would complement rather than replace coaching."The best coach will always beat AI. But the best coach using AI will beat the best coach not using AI," he said.The venture also plans to explore talent intelligence and live match analysis, including ball tracking and performance analytics for domestic competitions, leagues and broadcasters.Patel said his experience as a player, captain, scout and coach had reinforced the need for data to play a greater role in cricket.The venture, SportzEngage, is based in Bangalore. Its first application is called CRiQ.
Article Summary: Patel has worked with Mumbai Indians and Gujarat Titans in talent scouting and coaching after his playing career. He has teamed up with entrepreneurs Kunal Abhishek and Shamik Datta for the venture. The initiative aims to make performance analysis more accessible to cricketers.
